Rajkumar Balasaheb Sapate vs The State Of Maharashtra on 24
November, 2025

Author: Madhav J. Jamdar
Bench: Madhav J. Jamdar

In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Anticipatory Bail Application No. 2492 Of 2023
 Rajkumar Balasaheb Sapate ...Applican
 Versus
 The State of Maharashtra ...Responde

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Bombay
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Mr. Tushar Sonawane, for the Applicant.
Ms. R.V. Newton, App, for the Respondent-State.
Coram: Madhav J. Jamdar, J.

Dated : 24th November 2025
 Pc:-
 1. Heard Mr. Sonawane, learned Counsel appearing for the
 Applicant and Ms. Newton, learned App appearing for the
 Respondent-State.
 2.

By present Application, the Applicant is seeking pre-arrest  bail in connection with C.R. No. 112 of 2023 registered on 26 th  May 2023 under Sections 188, 272, 273, 328, 420, 465, 468, 471  read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("IPC") and  for the offence punishable under Sections 26(2)(i), 26(2)(ii),
26(2)(iv) 27(3)(e), 30(2)(a) and under Section 59 of the Food Rajkumar Balasaheb Sapate vs The State Of Maharashtra on 24 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147231088/
1  Safety and Standards Act, 2006 ("FSSA") with Igatpuri Police  Station, District Nashik (Rural).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the prosecution case the Applicant was dealing with  contraband material which is unsafe and dangerous for the health  of people.
4. It is the submission of Mr. Sonawane, learned Counsel that
except the offence under Section 328 of IPC, all other offences are  bailable offences.
He submits that as far as Section 328 of IPC is  concerned, the Supreme Court is considering the applicability of Section 328 of IPC to the similar cases.
He therefore, states that  the Anticipatory Bail be granted.
5. On the other hand, Ms. Newton, learned APP strongly  opposes the Anticipatory Bail Application.
She submits that the  offence is very serious and therefore, the Anticipatory Bail  Application be rejected.

Learned APP submits that there is one  antecedent being C.R. No.246 of 2020 registered on 03 rd October  2023 with Kasarvadawali Police Station, Thane for the offences  punishable under Sections 188, 269, 272, 273, 328 read with 34 of Rajkumar Balasaheb Sapate vs The State Of Maharashtra on 24 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147231088/
2 IPC, Section 51(b) of Disaster Management Act, 2005 and under Section 26(2)(i), 27(2)(e), 26(2)(iv), 30(2)(a) and 59 of the  FSSA.

sentences.text:
Learned APP submits that if this Court is inclined to grant  Anticipatory Bail then the Applicant be directed to give  undertaking in terms of order of the Supreme Court in the case of  Abhijit Jitendra Lolage vs State of Maharashtra 1 and more  particularly relies on following condition imposed by the Supreme  Court in case of similar offences :-
 "It is deemed appropriate to impose the  condition - "I, Abhijeet Jitendra Lolage do  undertake to not deal with Gutkha, that is, Pan  Masala with Tobacco".

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In case, the appellant -  Abhijeet Jitendra Lolage violates the terms and  conditions of bail, including the undertaking  imposed, it would be open to the prosecution to  seek cancellation of bail ".
(Emphasis added)
Mr. Sonawane, learned Counsel appearing for the Applicant after  taking the instructions submits that the Applicant will give the  undertaking.

Perusal of the record shows that except the offence under Section 328 of IPC the other offences are bailable offences.
The  issue whether Section 328 of IPC will apply to similar cases
is  pending before the Supreme Court.

There is one antecedent of  similar nature however the Applicant has been granted  Anticipatory Bail by learned Single Judge by order dated 19 th June  2023 passed in Anticipatory Bail Application No. 496 of 2023.
 9.
As the Applicant is ready to give the undertaking that he  will not deal with Gutkha and Tobacco products in any manner  whatsoever, the case is made out for grant of Anticipatory Bail.

10. In view thereof, the following order is passed:
 ORDER

4 (a) In the event of arrest of the Applicant- Rajkumar Balasaheb Sapate in connection with C.R.
No.112 of 2023 registered with the Igatpuri Police Station, District Nashik (Rural) the Applicant is directed to be released on bail on his furnishing P.R. Bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- with one or two solvent sureties in the like amount.
Page 4 603-ABA-2492-2023.ODT Akash Tayde
(b) The Applicant shall attend the concerned Police Station once in a month till filing of the chargesheet and shall cooperate with the investigation.

(c) The Applicant to furnish an undertaking that he will not deal with banned products i.e. Gutkha,
Pan Masala with Tobacco products in any manner whatsoever.
Such undertaking is to be filed in this Court within a period of two weeks from today.
The Applicant to strictly comply with the said undertaking.
(d) The Applicant shall furnish his cell phone number and residential address to the Investigating Officer and shall keep the same updated, in case of any change thereto.

(e) The Applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat, or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade such a person from disclosing the facts to the Court or to any Police personnel.
(f) The Applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence and shall not contact or influence the Page 5 603-ABA-2492-2023.ODT Akash Tayde Complainant or any witness in any manner.
(g) The Applicant shall not leave India without prior permission of the Court.
(h) In case, the Applicant violates the terms and conditions of bail, including the undertaking, it would be open to the prosecution to seek cancellation of bail.
11. The Anticipatory Bail Application is disposed of accordingly.
